newsitem.title: POLAND: KREDYT BANK SEEKS BANKING GROUP - PAPER.
newsitem.headline: KREDYT BANK SEEKS BANKING GROUP - PAPER.

text.p: Polish Kredyt Bank SA seeks to form a banking group containing two other banks currently listed on the Warsaw Stock Exchange, the daily Parkiet reported on Thursday.

"We plan to form a banking group with BPH , PBR, PBK and the Warta insurer ," Parkiet quoted Pacuk as saying, adding that Kredyt Bank would have to raise its capital to gain equal footing in the group.
Officials at the firms on Thursday either had no comment or were unavailable for comment.
On Wednesay Kredyt Bank shareholders approved an issue of 7.5 million to 10 million new shares to Powszechny Bank Kredytowy SA as part of the two banks' plan to exchange similar stakes.
Kredyt Bank has said the issue would be worth 37.5 million to 50 million zlotys.
Kredyt Bank seeks a 10-percent stake in PBK, whose privatisation is slated for the first half of next year.
PBK currently holds 4.4 million credit bank shares.
Bank Przemyslowo-Handlowy (BPH) has said it hopes to find a buyer for the treasury's current 46.6 percent stake in the first quarter of 1997.
PBK is Polish Development Bank's largest shareholder with 32.9 percent, followed by the treasury with 29.5 percent.

On Wednesday Kredyt Bank shareholders also approved an issue of 635,000 to 847,000 new shares worth 3.175 million to 4.235 million zlotys to the European Bank for Reconstruction and Development (EBRD) so as not to dilute the EBRD's stake.
The EBRD currently has two million Kredyt Bank shares.
